title: throughput-regression-continuous-batching-debug-notes
summary: Working notes: investigating throughput regression that started 2026-02-24; suspected continuous-batching config drift + KV cache eviction spike.
content:
Context:
- Regression observed 2026-02-24 ~15:30 UTC: average tokens/sec for text-gen p50 dropped from ~9k to ~3.2k on dedicated pool 'eu-west-1-ded-3'.
- Customer impact: increased tail latency, some 503s when autoscaler scaled down incorrectly.

Initial hypothesis:
- Continuous batching window got bumped (config drift) -> larger windows -> higher latency and less efficient batching -> lower throughput.
- Related: KV cache miss rate spiked (more cold starts for long conversations) causing higher per-request compute.

What I saw in metrics/logs:
- Prom metrics: runtime.batch_window_ms (observed) went from ~8ms -> 1200ms around 2026-02-24 15:17 UTC (exact point matches deployment window).
- kv_cache.hit_rate dropped from 0.94 -> 0.67 at same time.
- CPU/GPU utilization: GPU busy decreased from 78% -> 45% (indicating fewer tokens being produced across cluster), but pods' CPU spiked (scheduler thrash).
- Autoscaler events: scale-down at 15:22 triggered by pod liveness flapping; then scale up minutes later but capacity mismatch.

Commands / things I ran (breadcrumbs):
1) Pulled runtime config from cluster:
   kubectl -n runtime get cm runtime-config -o yaml | yq e .data.batch_config -
   -> saw continuous_batch.window_ms: 1200
2) Inspect recent commits to helm chart & config map:
   git log --since="2026-02-20" --pretty=oneline charts/runtime | sed -n '1,30p'
   -> found MR 789 (ops) that updated default batch window for high-latency NFS test but accidentally applied to prod values (missing env selector).
3) Replayed requests locally with micro-bench:
   python tools/microbench.py --model gptx-13b --qps 100 --seq 256 --batching continuous --window_ms 1200
   -> observed p50 token/sec ~3.1k, p95 latency 1.6s.
   python tools/microbench.py --window_ms 8
   -> p50 token/sec ~8.9k, p95 latency 220ms.
4) Checked runtime logs around 15:17:
   kubectl -n runtime logs -l app=runtime --since=60m | grep -i "batch window" -n
   -> repeated logs: "INFO continuous_batch: window_ms=1200 (env=prod) source=cm-update user=ops-bot"
5) KV cache metrics: instrumented via /metrics endpoint and traced requests with X-Request-ID:
   curl -s "http://runtime-metrics:9000/metrics" | grep kv_cache | sed -n '1,100p'
   -> kv_cache_hits_total increased slower than requests_total -> hit_rate drop consistent across nodes.
6) Heapster/allocator traces: noticed goroutine dumps showing more frequent small batches being sent out due to window expiry timers firing less often -> leads to fewer opportunities for coalescing.

Error snippets / logs (copied):
- "2026-02-24T15:17:02Z INFO continuous_batch: window_ms=1200 (env=prod) source=cm-update user=ops-bot"
- "2026-02-24T15:22:08Z WARN autoscaler: desired_replicas=1 actual=3 reason=scale_down (failed healthchecks)"
- "2026-02-24T15:23:10Z ERROR kvcache: evict: high_pressure:true evicted=10234"
- "2026-02-24T15:25:42Z ERROR http: upstream 503 code=503 msg=worker-no-capacity"

Immediate mitigations tried:
- Rollback CM to previous batch config (manual patch) and restarted runtime pods:
   kubectl -n runtime apply -f rollback-batch-window.yaml
   kubectl -n runtime rollout restart deployment/runtime --timeout=10m
  Result: partial recovery in ~3 minutes, p50 tokens/sec rose to ~7.5k but not fully to pre-incident 9k.
- Flushed KV cache on nodes to recover from pollution:
   curl -X POST http://runtime-admin:9001/kv/flush --data '{}'
  Result: kv cache hit_rate recovered to ~0.9 in ~10min. Throughput improved further to ~8.6k.

Root cause analysis (working):
- Primary: accidental change in continuous batching default (MR 789) applied to prod CM causing window_ms=1200. That reduced effective batching efficiency for our workload distribution (short requests benefit from small windows + continuous batching).
- Secondary: KV cache thrash due to higher latency + longer windows -> more unique KV states persist -> eviction pressure and miss rate spike.
- Tertiary: Autoscaler reaction to healthchecks and transient flapping exacerbated capacity shortages.

Hypotheses to validate:
- MR 789 lacked env=prod filter so a test tweak reached prod CM. Validate by checking CI/CD pipeline and chart templating logic. (Low friction fix: add validation to chart apply step).
- There might be a fallback in runtime to a global default when env var is missing (double-check code path runtime/config.go). If so, config drift could persist after CM rollback until pods restart.
- Autoscaler healthcheck sensitivity to slower startup path needs tuning; consider using readiness instead of liveness for short windows.

Next steps / TODOs:
- [ ] Create hotfix MR to restrict the chart value scope and add smoke test that validates batch window <= 50ms for prod envs (assigned to Priya). (JIRA-INC-423)
- [ ] Add an alert: if continuous_batch.window_ms > 100 then trigger paging (owner: Samir).
- [ ] Improve rollout playbook: sequence CM apply -> canary restart -> compare p50 throughput -> full rollout. Document in Confluence.
- [ ] Revisit autoscaler heuristics: don't scale down if recent 5m p95 latency > threshold. (SRE/ops)
- [ ] Add integration test in staging that runs microbench with typical short-seq workload and checks batch_window effect (tools/microbench).

Notes to self / small learnings:
- Continuous batching settings are very workload-sensitive: short-request-high-qps needs tiny window_ms to keep GPUs saturated.
- CM apply path needs guardrails; ops-bot bulk changes are dangerous when defaults are overwritten.
- When debugging throughput regressions, check batch window, kv_cache hit rate, autoscaler events (in that order).

Repro steps (minimal):
1) Apply configmap with continuous_batch.window_ms=1200 to a dedicated runtime cluster (staging).
2) Run tools/microbench.py with qps=100 seq=256 batching=continuous and compare token/sec vs baseline.
3) Observe kv cache metrics while running long conversation workload.

Quick commands to revert if seen in prod:
- kubectl -n runtime get cm runtime-config -o yaml > /tmp/runtime-config.yaml && edit window_ms -> 8 && kubectl apply -f /tmp/runtime-config.yaml
- kubectl -n runtime rollout restart deployment/runtime --timeout=10m
- curl -X POST http://runtime-admin:9001/kv/flush --data '{}'

If this reproduces, we can write a short postmortem for INC-423 and propose gating chart value changes behind a canary.

-- Alex M. (notes, messy)
